question: Whether WinINet's capture records an exchange WinINet makes over HTTP/2 as it records one over HTTP/1.1 - every part, numbered and flagged, in the same buffers - and what it keeps of heads that HTTP/2 frames and compresses.
answer: Its bodies as over HTTP/1.1: each as its client sent and read it, in the same buffers, numbered from 0 and flagged at its ends, nothing lost, every record the client process's; eight clients' exchanges multiplexed on one connection stay apart, each its own number. Its heads in HTTP/1.1's form, which no wire carried: a request head of the fields WinINet sent, named as WinINet names them and ending in the empty line, whose request line names HTTP/1.1; a response head whose status line names HTTP/1.1 and no reason, of the fields it received, named in lower case as HTTP/2 names them. No record says the exchange went over HTTP/2, so a head's version is WinINet's, not the protocol's.

probe.tool: tools/InterCat.WinInetProbe --http2 [--pace 5] [--async] [--gzip [--decode]] [--concurrency 8], 16 exchanges each or 64 eight at once, bodies up to 98,304 bytes, beside a decoy outside the process filter; the client enables HTTP/2 on its session and Kestrel offers it by ALPN over TLS, and both say each request went over HTTP/2

runs.run: HTTP/2, paced, eight at once, its buffers' metadata kept

capture.command: icat record --profile content --source etw/manifest/Microsoft-Windows-WinINet-Capture --mechanism http --pid <workload> --channel * --max-record-bytes 65536 --max-session-bytes 67108864 --inspection hex-text --duration 25, beside InterCat.TestWorkloads http-wininet --requests 64 --bytes 98304 --start-after 8 --http2 [--concurrency 8 --pace 5]; then icat exchanges --exchanges 10000 --decode, and each body saved by icat content --part and matched by SHA-256

ledger: fixtures/FX-HTTP-006/evidence/eight-at-once/buffers.csv: each buffer the probe captured of its 64 exchanges over one HTTP/2 connection, in time order - its 100 ns readings after the first, event, exchange number, place, ends, length, the request its exchange's head named, and whether a thread that made a request raised it - never its bytes. A test groups it as a session's records are grouped.
note: HTTP/2 has no message head on the wire: it carries the request line in pseudo-header fields and compresses every field, so the server's truth names each request's fields as it decoded them and each body as it read and wrote it, never a head's bytes, and a head kept is compared with it by its fields' names. Request 0's body is empty and raises no record; request 1's response is empty and is one buffer of no byte. Over HTTP/2 WinINet sent no Connection field, which HTTP/2 forbids, and HTTP/2 has no chunked transfer coding, so --chunked is refused with --http2.
